title: Why babies laugh, with Gina Mireault, PhD

sentences.en: Before babies have the words to tell us what they're thinking, they can laugh.
sentences.zh: 在婴儿学会用语言表达想法之前，他们就已经会笑了。

sentences.en: Infant giggles are undeniably adorable.
sentences.zh: 婴儿的咯咯笑声无疑是非常可爱的。

sentences.en: They're one of babyhood's most joyful milestones.
sentences.zh: 这是婴儿期最令人愉悦的里程碑之一。

sentences.en: And it turns out these joyful moments have a serious side too.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这些快乐的时刻也有其严肃的一面。

sentences.en: For scientists, infant laughter can provide a window into understanding how babies' minds develop during their first year of life.
sentences.zh: 对于科学家来说，婴儿的笑声可以为了解婴儿在出生第一年大脑如何发育提供一个窗口。

sentences.en: So when do babies start to laugh and why?
sentences.zh: 那么，婴儿从什么时候开始笑，又为什么会笑呢？

sentences.en: What do they find funny?
sentences.zh: 他们觉得什么是有趣的？

sentences.en: Why do some babies laugh at almost anything while others have a more serious temperament?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些婴儿几乎对什么都笑，而有些婴儿的性格却比较严肃？

sentences.en: When do babies start trying to make other people laugh?
sentences.zh: 婴儿从什么时候开始尝试逗别人笑？

sentences.en: And what can this progression tell us about babies' cognitive development and how they experience the world?
sentences.zh: 这种发展过程能告诉我们关于婴儿认知发展以及他们如何体验世界的什么信息？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Gina Moreau, a professor of psychology at Vermont State University, where she directs the Infant Laughter Lab.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是佛蒙特州立大学心理学教授吉娜·莫罗博士，她在那里负责婴儿笑声实验室。

sentences.en: She studies how babies discover what is funny, how they perceive, interpret, and respond to the unexpected in social contexts,
sentences.zh: 她研究婴儿如何发现有趣的事物，如何在社交环境中感知、解读并回应突发事件，

sentences.en: revealing the earliest foundations of humor and social understanding.
sentences.zh: 从而揭示了幽默和社会理解的最早基础。

sentences.en: Her research has been funded by the National Science Foundation and the National Institutes of Health and covered by media outlets, including CNN.com, NBC Nightly News,
sentences.zh: 她的研究得到了美国国家科学基金会和美国国立卫生研究院的资助，并被CNN.com、NBC晚间新闻等媒体报道，

sentences.en: and PBS's Nova Science Now.
sentences.zh: 以及PBS的《新星科学现在》节目。

sentences.en: She recently wrote an op-ed for the New York Times called The Evolutionary Brilliance of the Baby Giggle.
sentences.zh: 她最近为《纽约时报》撰写了一篇题为《婴儿咯咯笑的进化光辉》的评论文章。

sentences.en: Dr. Moreau, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 莫罗博士，感谢您今天参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: Let's start with the basics.
sentences.zh: 让我们从基础开始谈起。

sentences.en: How early do babies start to smile and laugh, and does smiling come first, or do both actions emerge around the same time?
sentences.zh: 婴儿多大开始微笑和大笑？是先有微笑，还是这两种行为几乎同时出现？

sentences.en: While smiling comes first, babies actually smile in utero.
sentences.zh: 微笑是先出现的，婴儿实际上在子宫里就会微笑。

sentences.en: So it's an involuntary smile, and most parents will observe this smile when their babies are brand new to the world.
sentences.zh: 那是一种无意识的微笑，大多数父母在宝宝刚出生时就会观察到这种微笑。

sentences.en: But these smiles are involuntary.
sentences.zh: 但这些微笑是无意识的。

sentences.en: They're not under the infant's control.
sentences.zh: 它们不受婴儿控制。

sentences.en: They smile in their sleep.
sentences.zh: 他们在睡梦中微笑。

sentences.en: They smile indiscriminately at any kind of stimulus.
sentences.zh: 他们会对任何刺激不加区分地微笑。

sentences.en: And it's not until about six weeks, but babies vary quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 直到大约六周大时，情况才有所改变，不过婴儿之间差异很大。

sentences.en: So some babies will start to voluntarily smile earlier than that.
sentences.zh: 所以有些婴儿会比这更早开始有意识地微笑。

sentences.en: But roughly about six weeks, babies can voluntarily smile.
sentences.zh: 但大约在六周左右，婴儿能够有意识地微笑。

sentences.en: So they become much more discriminating.
sentences.zh: 所以他们变得更有辨别力了。

sentences.en: They like faces, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们喜欢看人脸。

sentences.en: They might smile at the dog's face or at a lick from the dog or at mom or dad's voice or something like that.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会对着狗的脸笑，或者因为被狗舔了一下而笑，或者听到爸爸妈妈的声音而笑，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So six weeks, we see voluntary smiling.
sentences.zh: 所以六周时，我们看到了有意识的微笑。

sentences.en: And then laughter for most babies who are on a typical developmental trajectory is at about four months.
sentences.zh: 而对于大多数处于典型发育轨迹的婴儿来说，大笑大约出现在四个月大时。

sentences.en: Some babies a little sooner than that, and some babies a little later.
sentences.zh: 有些婴儿会早一点，有些会晚一点。

sentences.en: And what are the earliest things that make babies laugh?
sentences.zh: 那么，最早让婴儿大笑的事情是什么？

sentences.en: So typically, babies will respond to funny noises, unexpected noises.
sentences.zh: 通常，婴儿会对有趣的声音、意想不到的声音做出反应。

sentences.en: And they also respond to touch, so tickling, for example.
sentences.zh: 他们也会对触觉做出反应，比如挠痒痒。

sentences.en: You know, my son's first laugh was at my brother's sneeze, which is a shocking sneeze.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我儿子的第一次大笑是因为我哥哥打了个喷嚏，那是一个很惊人的喷嚏。

sentences.en: So it is a sneeze that will get your attention.
sentences.zh: 那是一个会引起你注意的喷嚏。

sentences.en: And so it might be something like that, hearing a rooster crow or something that's really novel that they've never heard before.
sentences.zh: 所以可能是类似的事情，听到公鸡打鸣，或者听到他们从未听过的新奇事物。

sentences.en: That will often do it for a brand new laugher.
sentences.zh: 这通常会让刚学会大笑的婴儿笑出来。

sentences.en: Now, in adults, we know that laughter is one way that we bond with other people.
sentences.zh: 在成年人中，我们知道笑是我们与他人建立联系的一种方式。

sentences.en: What purpose does laughter serve in babies?
sentences.zh: 笑对婴儿有什么作用？

sentences.en: Is it the same for babies as it is for adults?
sentences.zh: 对婴儿来说，笑的作用和对成年人一样吗？

sentences.en: We think so.
sentences.zh: 我们认为是这样的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think one of the surprising things about laughter and smiling is that, laughter in particular,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为关于笑和微笑，令人惊讶的一点是，尤其是笑，

sentences.en: is that there's really good research, primarily initiated by Robert Provine at the University of Maryland, showing that laughter in adults rarely follows a joke.
sentences.zh: 有非常好的研究，主要是由马里兰大学的罗伯特·普罗文发起的，表明成年人的笑很少是因为笑话。

sentences.en: So it's not that we don't laugh at jokes.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我们不对笑话发笑。

sentences.en: We do.
sentences.zh: 我们会的。

sentences.en: But most of our laughter is in response to these benign social remarks, like,
sentences.zh: 但我们大部分的笑是对这些温和的社交言论的回应，比如，

sentences.en: oh, I'm going to be late, ha, ha, ha, ha, or oh, I parked the car funny, ha, ha, ha, ha, or something like that, like, or I can't find my keys, ha, ha, ha.
sentences.zh: 哦，我要迟到了，哈哈哈哈，或者哦，我停车停得真滑稽，哈哈哈哈，或者类似的事情，比如，我找不到钥匙了，哈哈哈哈。

sentences.en: So these are odd things that we laugh at.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是我们发笑的奇怪事情。

sentences.en: But in keeping with Darwin's idea, Darwin was the first one to really write about infant laughter in his own child.
sentences.zh: 但秉承达尔文的观点，达尔文是第一个真正记录自己孩子笑声的人。

sentences.en: The idea is that laughter and smiling is a social signal, primarily.
sentences.zh: 这个观点是，笑和微笑主要是一种社交信号。

sentences.en: It serves a social purpose, first and foremoSt.
sentences.zh: 它首先且最重要的是服务于社交目的。

sentences.en: We do share these kinds of signals with other mammals.
sentences.zh: 我们确实与其他哺乳动物共享这些信号。

sentences.en: So it does seem to communicate, I trust you, we are safe together, I enjoy your company, I like you, those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 所以它似乎确实在传达：我相信你，我们在一起很安全，我喜欢你的陪伴，我喜欢你，诸如此类的信息。

sentences.en: Understanding a joke is a cognitive exercise.
sentences.zh: 理解一个笑话是一种认知练习。

sentences.en: You have to get why a joke is funny to laugh at it.
sentences.zh: 你必须明白为什么一个笑话好笑才会发笑。

sentences.en: But in your work, you found that infants as young as four to five months can distinguish between ordinary and incongruous events, and they find incongruous things funny.
sentences.zh: 但在你的工作中，你发现四到五个月大的婴儿就能区分普通事件和不协调事件，而且他们觉得不协调的事情很有趣。

sentences.en: Tell us about that work.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲那项工作吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, this still knocks my socks off.
sentences.zh: 是的，这至今仍让我感到震惊。

sentences.en: I mean, I think this is what I love about science is science is so surprising.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这就是我热爱科学的原因，科学是如此令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Whether you get the hypothesis right or not, there's always something there to unpack.
sentences.zh: 无论你的假设是否正确，总有一些东西值得去挖掘。

sentences.en: So we really thought that this was kind of an open and shut case when we were trying to figure out why do babies or how do they figure out what's funny.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们试图弄清楚婴儿为什么或如何发现什么是好笑的时候，我们真的以为这是一个简单明了的问题。

sentences.en: And typically what happens is, you know, parents are giving lots of cues when there are these absurd things going on.
sentences.zh: 通常发生的情况是，你知道，当这些荒谬的事情发生时，父母会给出很多暗示。

sentences.en: So the parent blows a raspberry on the baby's tummy and laughs and smiles in response.
sentences.zh: 比如父母在婴儿肚子上吹气发出噗噗声，并做出回应，大笑和微笑。

sentences.en: Or they pull their socks off and wave them around and laugh and smile while they're doing that.
sentences.zh: 或者他们脱下袜子挥舞，同时大笑和微笑。

sentences.en: And we thought, well, this is what's going on, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们想，嗯，这就是发生的事情，你知道。

sentences.en: So we set up a little comedy club for babies in their homes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在婴儿家中为他们建立了一个小型喜剧俱乐部。

sentences.en: And we showed babies two different types of absurd events.
sentences.zh: 我们向婴儿展示了两种不同类型的荒谬事件。

sentences.en: One was taking a foam ball and putting it on the research assistant's nose.
sentences.zh: 一种是拿一个泡沫球放在研究助理的鼻子上。

sentences.en: And the research assistant would poke their nose with their finger and say, beep, beep, beep, all with a straight face.
sentences.zh: 研究助理会用手指戳鼻子说，哔，哔，哔，全程面无表情。

sentences.en: The control event was the same foam ball that the researcher just passed back and forth from hand to hand while they said a script.
sentences.zh: 对照事件是同一个泡沫球，研究人员只是在手中来回传递，同时念着台词。

sentences.en: Like, this is a ball, it's red, it's squishy, something like that.
sentences.zh: 比如，这是一个球，它是红色的，它是软的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And then we had parents do one of two things.
sentences.zh: 然后我们让父母做两件事中的一件。

sentences.en: So the parents never interacted with the infant.
sentences.zh: 父母从不与婴儿互动。

sentences.en: The infant could see the parent and the research assistant.
sentences.zh: 婴儿可以看到父母和研究助理。

sentences.en: And the infants were really poised so they could see the parent's reaction to the event.
sentences.zh: 婴儿被安置得很好，所以他们可以看到父母对事件的反应。

sentences.en: And so when the odd event was shown, like the ball is the clown nose, parents were instructed to either point and laugh at the clown nose or to simply look at it,
sentences.zh: 所以当奇怪的事件出现时，比如球变成了小丑鼻子，父母被指示要么指着小丑鼻子大笑，要么只是看着它，

sentences.en: to not laugh or smile, just have a neutral face.
sentences.zh: 不笑也不微笑，只是保持中立的表情。

sentences.en: And we really thought these six-month-olds would just find it funny when the parents found it funny.
sentences.zh: 我们真的以为这些六个月大的婴儿只有在父母觉得好笑时才会觉得好笑。

sentences.en: But that's not what we observed.
sentences.zh: 但我们观察到的并非如此。

sentences.en: So the six-month-olds were much more sophisticated than we thought.
sentences.zh: 所以六个月大的婴儿比我们想象的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: This is often the case when you're studying babies, and parents know this, grandparents know this, babies will surprise you at their level of sophistication.
sentences.zh: 当你研究婴儿时，这种情况经常发生，父母知道这一点，祖父母也知道这一点，婴儿的复杂程度会让你大吃一惊。

sentences.en: So the six-month-olds were actually more likely to laugh at the event when the parents stayed out of it.
sentences.zh: 所以当父母不参与时，六个月大的婴儿实际上更有可能对事件发笑。

sentences.en: So they were decoding this event all by themselves as being silly.
sentences.zh: 所以他们完全是靠自己解读这个事件是滑稽的。

sentences.en: And it's still surprising to me that this is the case.
sentences.zh: 直到现在，这种情况对我来说仍然很令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Now, when do babies start trying to be funny themselves, to produce humor rather than just laugh at something?
sentences.zh: 那么，婴儿从什么时候开始尝试自己变得滑稽，去制造幽默而不仅仅是对某事发笑？

sentences.en: And what does that say about their cognitive development at that point?
sentences.zh: 这说明了他们当时的认知发展情况如何？

sentences.en: It's such a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: And what this question really gets at is intentionality.
sentences.zh: 这个问题真正触及的是意图性。

sentences.en: So when is it that babies intend to make somebody else laugh?
sentences.zh: 那么，婴儿在什么时候打算让别人发笑呢？

sentences.en: And that can be a really tricky thing to get at experimentally.
sentences.zh: 在实验中要弄清楚这一点可能是一件非常棘手的事情。

sentences.en: We also know that babies will accidentally make people laugh.
sentences.zh: 我们也知道婴儿会无意中让人发笑。

sentences.en: So, for example, babies don't have a lot of good physical control over their bodies in the first few months.
sentences.zh: 例如，婴儿在最初几个月对身体的物理控制能力并不强。

sentences.en: So at three months or three and a half months, they might make a strange face, or maybe their eyes are going in two different directions, or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以在三个月或三个半月大时，他们可能会做一个奇怪的表情，或者眼睛可能向两个不同的方向看，诸如此类。

sentences.en: It's not their fault.
sentences.zh: 这不是他们的错。

sentences.en: They just aren't myelinated yet.
sentences.zh: 他们只是还没有髓鞘化。

sentences.en: So parents might laugh at these odd things that babies are doing, which aren't under infant's control.
sentences.zh: 所以父母可能会对婴儿做的这些奇怪的事情发笑，而这些事情并不受婴儿控制。

sentences.en: We are too conservative as scientists to attribute intentionality to that.
sentences.zh: 作为科学家，我们太保守了，不会把意图性归因于此。

sentences.en: What we do know, though, is that by about five months, babies do start to imitate odd actions.
sentences.zh: 不过我们确实知道，到五个月左右，婴儿确实开始模仿奇怪的动作。

sentences.en: So, for example, if parents are just blowing raspberries, babies will typically have enough voluntary control to participate in that and to maybe imitate that as well.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果父母只是吹气发出噗噗声，婴儿通常会有足够的自主控制能力参与其中，甚至可能模仿这一点。

sentences.en: We've seen infants in our studies do this.
sentences.zh: 我们在研究中见过婴儿这样做。

sentences.en: And parents, of course, will laugh at that.
sentences.zh: 当然，父母会对此发笑。

sentences.en: So I think it's a very dynamic process where babies figure out what gets the caregiver's attention and keeps it and is fun and enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一个非常动态的过程，婴儿会弄清楚什么能引起照顾者的注意，保持这种注意，并且是有趣和令人愉快的。

sentences.en: Certainly by six months, babies are acting with intention.
sentences.zh: 到六个月大时，婴儿肯定是有意图地行动了。

sentences.en: They will knock over a sibling's tower on purpose, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们会故意推倒兄弟姐妹的积木塔。

sentences.en: There's a great viral video on YouTube of a dad tearing paper.
sentences.zh: YouTube上有一个很火的视频，是一位父亲在撕纸。

sentences.en: And the baby sitting on the couch seems to be about six or seven months old.
sentences.zh: 坐在沙发上的婴儿看起来大约六七个月大。

sentences.en: And the dad tears the paper and the baby just cracks up and just can't contain themselves.
sentences.zh: 父亲撕纸，婴儿就笑得前仰后合，无法自控。

sentences.en: And this is a good example of what we call violating construction.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的例子，我们称之为违反结构。

sentences.en: So this paper is supposed to be in a certain form and the dad is destroying it.
sentences.zh: 这张纸本应保持某种形式，而父亲正在破坏它。

sentences.en: And we see infants start doing that at about six months of age where they will violate a construction, pop a bubble on purpose, for example, something like that.
sentences.zh: 我们看到婴儿在六个月大时开始这样做，他们会违反结构，比如故意戳破一个泡泡，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Will babies smile or laugh when they're alone?
sentences.zh: 婴儿独自一人时会微笑或大笑吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I think we know that adults don't tend to do this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我们知道成年人通常不会这样做。

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: There's just a little bit of research on this.
sentences.zh: 关于这方面的研究很少。

sentences.en: There's just so little research in this area.
sentences.zh: 这个领域的研究实在太少了。

sentences.en: So if anyone out there is thinking about a dissertation topic, look me up.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人在考虑论文题目，可以找我。

sentences.en: There is some work by Marianne LaFrance with 10-month-olds.
sentences.zh: 玛丽安·拉弗朗斯对10个月大的婴儿做过一些研究。

sentences.en: And I don't remember exactly the experimental setup, but she did observe that infants were much less likely to smile when they were by themselves than when there was a caregiver.
sentences.zh: 我不记得确切的实验设置，但她确实观察到，婴儿独自一人时比有照顾者在场时微笑的可能性要小得多。

sentences.en: And it doesn't take much.
sentences.zh: 而且不需要太多条件。

sentences.en: Like with babies that are about three months of age, our first study found that about 50% of three-month-olds would smile simply in response to a caregiver's smile.
sentences.zh: 比如对于大约三个月大的婴儿，我们的第一项研究发现，大约50%的三个月大的婴儿仅仅是为了回应照顾者的微笑而微笑。

sentences.en: But by six months, only about 5% of babies would do that.
sentences.zh: 但到了六个月大时，只有大约5%的婴儿会这样做。

sentences.en: So smiling alone is not quite enough.
sentences.zh: 所以独自微笑是不够的。

sentences.en: There is this cognitive piece that is involved a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 稍后会涉及到一个认知部分。

sentences.en: But you're asking a really insightful question, which is that, yes, smiling does seem to be
sentences.zh: 但你问了一个非常有见地的问题，那就是，是的，微笑似乎确实是

sentences.en: this social signal so that if you're by yourself, you might as well reserve your smiling.
sentences.zh: 这种社交信号，所以如果你独自一人，你最好还是保留你的微笑。

sentences.en: What if a baby doesn't start laughing around five months or so?
sentences.zh: 如果婴儿在五个月左右还没有开始大笑怎么办？

sentences.en: What does that indicate?
sentences.zh: 这说明了什么？

sentences.en: And when should a parent be concerned?
sentences.zh: 父母什么时候应该担心？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: I'm not a pediatrician or a clinician, so I'm always a little bit hesitant.
sentences.zh: 我不是儿科医生或临床医生，所以我总是有点犹豫。

sentences.en: I get a lot of emails from parents who are worried.
sentences.zh: 我收到很多担心的父母发来的电子邮件。

sentences.en: And I tend to think that parents and other caregivers should go on their gut instinct here.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于认为父母和其他照顾者应该相信自己的直觉。

sentences.en: They have the best experience with their baby.
sentences.zh: 他们对自己的宝宝最有经验。

sentences.en: They have the best frame of reference for what their infant does.
sentences.zh: 他们对婴儿的行为有最好的参考框架。

sentences.en: Do they make eye contact, for example?
sentences.zh: 例如，他们有眼神交流吗？

sentences.en: Do they like to be snuggled?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢被拥抱吗？

sentences.en: Are they curious and investigating the environment?
sentences.zh: 他们对环境感到好奇并进行探索吗？

sentences.en: So is this lack of laughter sort of part of a bigger picture?
sentences.zh: 所以这种缺乏笑声是否是更大图景的一部分？

sentences.en: Or is it just this thing where it takes more to get them to laugh?
sentences.zh: 还是说这只是需要更多努力才能让他们笑出来的情况？

sentences.en: We've done one study looking at laughter at six months as a predictor of attachment at one year.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一项研究，观察六个月大的笑声作为一岁时依恋关系的预测指标。

sentences.en: And so this was a longitudinal study.
sentences.zh: 这是一项纵向研究。

sentences.en: And again, we were really surprised at the findings.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们对结果感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: We actually found that babies who had a higher threshold to laughing, so they weren't big laughers.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上发现，那些笑声阈值较高的婴儿，也就是说他们不是爱笑的人。

sentences.en: They weren't laughing with the frequency of some of their counterparts in our sample.
sentences.zh: 他们笑的频率并没有我们样本中其他一些同龄婴儿那么高。

sentences.en: They actually had a higher quality of attachment at 12 months.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他们在12个月大时表现出了更高质量的依恋关系。

sentences.en: And it's very counterintuitive.
sentences.zh: 这非常反直觉。

sentences.en: But we think what was happening is that parents of these more sober babies had to work harder to get them to smile and to engage with them.
sentences.zh: 但我们认为发生的情况是，这些比较沉稳的婴儿的父母，必须付出更多努力才能逗他们笑，并与他们互动。

sentences.en: And that this actually paid dividends for the babies in terms of attachment.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上在依恋关系方面为婴儿带来了回报。

sentences.en: Do you follow babies very far into their lives?
sentences.zh: 你们会长期追踪婴儿的成长吗？

sentences.en: I mean, like, do you know if you're looking at a baby at four or five months, do you ever see that same child at five and discover whether, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你观察一个四五个月大的婴儿，你以后还会见到同一个孩子，并发现他是否，你知道，

sentences.en: this kid's a stand-up comedian.
sentences.zh: 是个脱口秀演员吗？

sentences.en: He was very funny as a baby.
sentences.zh: 他婴儿时期就很有趣。

sentences.en: We don't.
sentences.zh: 我们不会。

sentences.en: It's hard enough to follow them for a couple of months.
sentences.zh: 追踪他们几个月就已经够难了。

sentences.en: Babies are actually very hard to study because parents are so busy.
sentences.zh: 婴儿其实很难研究，因为父母太忙了。

sentences.en: And babies often are cutting teeth or they get sick or they just don't feel like participating in your study the day you need them to laugh.
sentences.zh: 而且婴儿经常长牙、生病，或者在你需要他们笑的那天，他们就是不想配合你的研究。

sentences.en: They're in a terrible mood.
sentences.zh: 他们心情很糟糕。

sentences.en: So we do well to follow them.
sentences.zh: 所以我们能追踪他们就已经很不错了。

sentences.en: You know, we've done only one study where we followed them from three months to 12 months.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们只做过一项研究，追踪了他们从3个月到12个月大的过程。

sentences.en: And it was incredibly laborious.
sentences.zh: 那真是极其费力。

sentences.en: We're glad we did it.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴做了这项研究。

sentences.en: But yet, right now, we're just doing some point-in-time studies.
sentences.zh: 但目前，我们只是在做一些横断面研究。

sentences.en: But we have done some from six to 12 months.
sentences.zh: 不过我们确实做过一些从6个月到12个月的研究。

sentences.en: Usually, I don't go past that point.
sentences.zh: 通常，我不会超过那个时间点。

sentences.en: I have a great colleague at the University of Bristol in the UK who studies joke telling in toddlers.
sentences.zh: 我在英国布里斯托大学有一位很棒的同事，她专门研究幼儿讲笑话。

sentences.en: So she sort of picks up where I left off or vice versa.
sentences.zh: 所以她算是接手了我未完成的工作，反之亦然。

sentences.en: Are there cultural differences or do all babies manifest humor at about the same time developmentally and in response to the same stimuli?
sentences.zh: 是否存在文化差异？还是说所有婴儿在发育过程中大约在同一时间，并对相同的刺激做出幽默反应？

sentences.en: We don't have great cross-cultural data.
sentences.zh: 我们没有很好的跨文化数据。

sentences.en: I mean, I tend to think about laughter and humor are separate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我倾向于认为笑声和幽默是两回事。

sentences.en: So laughter, I think, we can think of as following a developmental trajectory that's probably not culture-bound.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，我们可以把笑声看作是遵循一种可能不受文化限制的发育轨迹。

sentences.en: It's kind of like walking and talking that these milestones tend to be hit at about the same ages unless there's some extreme intervention on part of the culture.
sentences.zh: 这有点像走路和说话，除非文化上有某种极端的干预，否则这些里程碑通常会在差不多的年龄达到。

sentences.en: There's, for example, a culture where they use cradleboarding and babies are strapped to a cradleboard while their parents work in the fields.
sentences.zh: 例如，有一种文化会使用摇篮板，当父母在田里干活时，婴儿就被绑在摇篮板上。

sentences.en: And those babies are a little later to walk.
sentences.zh: 那些婴儿走路会晚一点。

sentences.en: But as soon as they're out of the cradleboard, they catch right up with their peers.
sentences.zh: 但一旦他们离开摇篮板，他们很快就能赶上同龄人。

sentences.en: So I think we can think of laughter as being not culture-bound.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们可以认为笑声是不受文化限制的。

sentences.en: Humor might be.
sentences.zh: 幽默可能受限制。

sentences.en: And that might also include the culture of the family, not just the culture of the country or the nation.
sentences.zh: 这可能也包括家庭文化，而不仅仅是国家或民族的文化。

sentences.en: So I think about the type of things that kids are allowed to laugh at, for example.
sentences.zh: 所以我考虑的是孩子们被允许笑的事情类型，举个例子。

sentences.en: In my own family, we tend to say we have very dark humor.
sentences.zh: 在我自己的家庭里，我们倾向于说我们有非常暗黑的幽默感。

sentences.en: And our kids who are now adults had and still have very dark humor.
sentences.zh: 我们的孩子现在已经是成年人了，他们过去有，现在依然有非常暗黑的幽默感。

sentences.en: And we saw that from them at very early ages.
sentences.zh: 我们很早就从他们身上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And we even wondered, as parents, we're both psychologists, is that okay?
sentences.zh: 作为父母，我们俩都是心理学家，我们甚至会想，这没问题吗？

sentences.en: But we decided we had other things to worry about.
sentences.zh: 但我们决定还有其他事情要担心。

sentences.en: So I think that humor specifically probably is culture-bound.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为幽默具体来说可能确实是受文化限制的。

sentences.en: And the culture can be a microculture of the family or a community, for example.
sentences.zh: 而这种文化可以是家庭或社区的微观文化，例如。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们要休息一下。

sentences.en: When we get back, we'll talk about whether there are any surefire jokes that make all babies laugh.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将讨论是否有任何能让所有婴儿发笑的万无一失的笑话。

sentences.en: Is there any one thing that all babies find funny, like peekaboo?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么东西是所有婴儿都觉得好笑的，比如躲猫猫？

sentences.en: Well, I never like to say all, but I think peekaboo is a great guess.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我从不喜欢说“所有”，但我认为躲猫猫是一个很好的猜测。

sentences.en: If you are traveling on public transportation and there's an infant whose parent really needs a break,
sentences.zh: 如果你在乘坐公共交通工具，而有个婴儿的父母真的很需要休息一下，

sentences.en: then I think peekaboo is a great go-to.
sentences.zh: 那么我认为躲猫猫是一个很好的选择。

sentences.en: And babies in the four- to six-month-old age range, our pediatrician used to say they have a social agenda.
sentences.zh: 对于4到6个月大的婴儿，我们的儿科医生过去常说他们有“社交议程”。

sentences.en: I love that description, that they are so engaged by other people for the most part, they might find almost anything you offer them to be worthy of a smile, if not a laugh.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个描述，他们在很大程度上被其他人所吸引，他们可能会觉得你提供的几乎任何东西都值得一笑，即使不是大笑。

sentences.en: Peekaboo is great.
sentences.zh: 躲猫猫很棒。

sentences.en: Tickling tends to be a universal crowd pleaser for infants.
sentences.zh: 挠痒痒往往是婴儿通用的“取悦大众”的方式。

sentences.en: Certainly infants under about seven or eight months, they like it.
sentences.zh: 当然，7或8个月以下的婴儿，他们喜欢这样。

sentences.en: But we do know that as babies get older, for example, even by six months, babies will find peekaboo entertaining for a very short period of time.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实知道，随着婴儿长大，例如到了6个月大，婴儿只会觉得躲猫猫在很短的时间内有趣。

sentences.en: And then you need to work harder to keep them engaged.
sentences.zh: 然后你需要更努力地让他们保持参与。

sentences.en: So they start doing something fascinating at that point, which is something called polite laughter, which is also sometimes referred to as fake laughter.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在那个时候开始做一件令人着迷的事情，那就是所谓的“礼貌性笑声”，有时也被称为“假笑”。

sentences.en: So I don't like fake because it sounds manipulative, but that is what it's called in the literature.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢“假”这个词，因为它听起来有操纵性，但文献中确实是这样称呼的。

sentences.en: So this just means that adults do this too.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是意味着成年人也会这样做。

sentences.en: If we, you know, somebody tells a joke and we think it's kind of funny, we might go, you know, something like that, where we want to communicate, like, we really like you
sentences.zh: 如果有人讲了个笑话，我们觉得还行，我们可能会发出那种声音，你知道，类似那样，我们想传达的是，我们真的很喜欢你，

sentences.en: and we really want to stay in this conversation with you, but you got to do better.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很想继续和你聊天，但你得讲得更好一点。

sentences.en: Six-month-olds can do that.
sentences.zh: 6个月大的婴儿就能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What about other mammals?
sentences.zh: 那其他哺乳动物呢？

sentences.en: Do other mammals smile and laugh like human babies?
sentences.zh: 其他哺乳动物会像人类婴儿一样微笑和发笑吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they do.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们会。

sentences.en: And this is so amazing, particularly juveniles.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了，尤其是幼崽。

sentences.en: So most of this work, there's some good work in comparative psychology, looking at this and other non-human primates.
sentences.zh: 大部分这方面的研究，在比较心理学中有一些很好的工作，观察了这一点以及其他非人类灵长类动物。

sentences.en: But I think some of the most fascinating work was by Yak Pengsep, who just passed away within the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: 但我认为最引人入胜的一些工作是由雅克·潘克塞普（Jaak Panksepp）完成的，他刚在过去几年去世了。

sentences.en: He was a neuroscientist and he studied rats and found kind of by accident that when you tickle rats, he studied emotions.
sentences.zh: 他是一位神经科学家，他研究老鼠，并偶然发现当你挠老鼠痒时——他研究的是情绪。

sentences.en: So there was a reason for him to be doing this.
sentences.zh: 所以他做这个是有原因的。

sentences.en: When you tickle rats, they actually chirp and they chirp at a very high frequency.
sentences.zh: 当你挠老鼠痒时，它们实际上会发出啁啾声，而且频率非常高。

sentences.en: So it's not available to the human ear.
sentences.zh: 所以人耳是听不到的。

sentences.en: You have to have specialized equipment to hear it.
sentences.zh: 你必须有专门的设备才能听到。

sentences.en: But their chirping is at a similar cadence to human laughter.
sentences.zh: 但它们的啁啾声节奏与人类的笑声相似。

sentences.en: For listeners who have dogs, dogs are a great example.
sentences.zh: 对于有狗的听众来说，狗就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: If you listen to dogs when they're playing, they do what's called play panting.
sentences.zh: 如果你听狗玩耍时的声音，它们会发出所谓的“玩耍喘息声”。

sentences.en: And it sounds kind of like a chimp.
sentences.zh: 听起来有点像黑猩猩。

sentences.en: So they go, they only do this on the exhale.
sentences.zh: 它们只在呼气时发出这种声音。

sentences.en: But anyway, dogs do this and other mammals do as well.
sentences.zh: 总之，狗会这样，其他哺乳动物也会。

sentences.en: So again, this kind of gives some real leverage to Darwin's argument.
sentences.zh: 所以这再次为达尔文的论点提供了一些真正的支持。

sentences.en: What Pengsep discovered, he may not be the first to discover this, but I can credit it
sentences.zh: 潘克塞普发现的——他可能不是第一个发现这一点的人，但我可以自信地归功于他——

sentences.en: to him with confidence, is that other mammals have all the same brain structures of the limbic system, which we have.
sentences.zh: 是其他哺乳动物拥有与我们相同的边缘系统大脑结构。

sentences.en: So all mammals share those same structures.
sentences.zh: 所以所有哺乳动物都共享这些相同的结构。

sentences.en: And that suggests that emotion, joy, sadness, some of the primary emotions did not just bubble
sentences.zh: 这表明情绪、快乐、悲伤，一些基本情绪不仅仅是在人类身上突然出现的，

sentences.en: up in humans, that these have been there and they're part of our evolutionary ancestry.
sentences.zh: 这些情绪一直存在，是我们进化祖先的一部分。

sentences.en: So we're not necessarily projecting onto our pets that they're laughing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不一定是在把它们在笑投射到我们的宠物身上。

sentences.en: They may actually be laughing in their own way.
sentences.zh: 它们可能真的在以自己的方式发笑。

sentences.en: I live with a very funny dog.
sentences.zh: 我住在一起的狗就非常有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think, you know, we have to be careful about that, right?
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，我们必须小心这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: That we're not just projecting.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅仅是在投射。

sentences.en: Although Pengsep actually made the argument that we should, that to try to remove ourselves
sentences.zh: 尽管潘克塞普实际上提出了一个观点，认为我们应该这样做，试图将我们自己从其他哺乳动物的体验中剥离出来，

sentences.en: from the other mammalian experience is really inhumane and it's ascientific or non-scientific,
sentences.zh: 实际上是不人道的，也是非科学的，

sentences.en: that to understand other emotional experience, we should try to relate it to our own experience.
sentences.zh: 为了理解其他情感体验，我们应该尝试将其与我们自己的体验联系起来。

sentences.en: This was not necessarily a popular argument.
sentences.zh: 这不一定是一个受欢迎的观点。

sentences.en: It was a very controversial argument to make, but it's an interesting one to entertain.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有争议的观点，但值得探讨。

sentences.en: So how did you get interested in studying humor in babies and has it been challenging for you?
sentences.zh: 那么你是如何对研究婴儿幽默产生兴趣的？这对你来说有挑战性吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you've got a lab, but getting funding for the kind of research you do, which some people might say is frivolous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有一个实验室，但为你所做的这种研究获得资金，有些人可能会说这是轻浮的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So for about 15 years, I studied loss.
sentences.zh: 所以大约有15年的时间，我研究的是丧失。

sentences.en: I studied early loss in childhood.
sentences.zh: 我研究的是童年早期的丧失。

sentences.en: And at the beginning of that line of research, I had a baby and I had never, my son's my first born and I had never even changed a diaper.
sentences.zh: 在那项研究刚开始时，我生了一个孩子，我从来没有——我儿子是我的第一个孩子，我甚至从来没换过尿布。

sentences.en: It's a, it's a shock that they let me leave the hospital with him.
sentences.zh: 他们让我带着他离开医院，这真是个震惊。

sentences.en: We had no experience, but anyway, it was, so I was really, you know, having this front seat experience with him as a mom.
sentences.zh: 我们没有任何经验，但总之，作为一名母亲，我确实亲身体验了这一切。

sentences.en: And he started laughing to my brother's sneeze when he was about three and a half months old.
sentences.zh: 当他大约3个半月大时，他开始对着我哥哥的喷嚏笑。

sentences.en: And, you know, when you're a psychologist, you just can't help but observe behavior.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当你是一名心理学家时，你忍不住会观察行为。

sentences.en: It's just kind of an occupational hazard.
sentences.zh: 这算是一种职业病。

sentences.en: Um, and I remember being so shocked that he was laughing and really amused and entertained by this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得当时非常震惊，他竟然在笑，而且真的被这个逗乐了。

sentences.en: And I, I thought, what is that?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，那是什么？

sentences.en: Why, why, why do infants laugh?
sentences.zh: 为什么，为什么，为什么婴儿会笑？

sentences.en: I knew that they laughed.
sentences.zh: 我知道他们会笑。

sentences.en: I just never asked the question why.
sentences.zh: 我只是从来没问过为什么。

sentences.en: So it was about, he was 13 when I took a sabbatical and switched my research focus, um, and went and studied in the UK with my colleague now, good friend, Vasu Reddy.
sentences.zh: 所以大约在他13岁时，我休了学术假，转换了我的研究重点，去英国和我现在的同事、好朋友瓦苏·雷迪（Vasu Reddy）一起学习。

sentences.en: And it was at that point I had to apply for funding.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我不得不申请资金。

sentences.en: So I was really worried that this would be seen as a frivolous line of research.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很担心这会被视为一项轻浮的研究。

sentences.en: Um, I applied for some funding within my state, uh, in Vermont, we have this nice mechanism
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在我所在的州申请了一些资金，在佛蒙特州，我们有一个很好的机制，

sentences.en: that is through an NIH INBRI grant so that little colleges don't have to compete with the big colleges for money.
sentences.zh: 是通过NIH的INBRI拨款，这样小学院就不必和大大学竞争资金了。

sentences.en: So I got a little grant and collected some data with my students.
sentences.zh: 所以我得到了一小笔资助，并和我的学生收集了一些数据。

sentences.en: And then I went to a big infancy conference to present it.
sentences.zh: 然后我去了一个大型婴儿会议上展示它。

sentences.en: And I was very, very nervous.
sentences.zh: 我当时非常非常紧张。

sentences.en: And the very first response I got, I was just doing a poster because it was some preliminary data.
sentences.zh: 我得到的第一个回应——我当时只是在展示海报，因为那是一些初步数据——

sentences.en: Uh, another scientist approached me and she said, oh my gosh, you study laughing?
sentences.zh: 另一位科学家走近我，她说，天哪，你研究笑？

sentences.en: Oh, I study crying.
sentences.zh: 哦，我研究哭。

sentences.en: She was, she was so filled with regret.
sentences.zh: 她当时充满了遗憾。

sentences.en: And, you know, she really, um, ah, she just gave me this sense of real relief and validation that, okay, it's going to be okay.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，她真的给了我一种真正的解脱感和认可感，觉得，好吧，没关系。

sentences.en: She was fascinated in the study.
sentences.zh: 她对这项研究很着迷。

sentences.en: So from that point on, I was never concerned.
sentences.zh: 所以从那时起，我就再也不担心了。

sentences.en: And the work has been wonderfully received, um, everywhere that I've presented it or my students have presented it.
sentences.zh: 这项工作在任何我展示过或我的学生展示过的地方都受到了极好的欢迎。

sentences.en: In terms of getting funding, um, I will say that I don't use the words humor.
sentences.zh: 在获得资金方面，嗯，我会说我不用“幽默”这个词。

sentences.en: I don't use, we do say that we measure laughter, but, um, you know, it's what we're really studying
sentences.zh: 我不用，我们确实说我们测量笑声，但是，嗯，你知道，我们真正研究的是

sentences.en: was something you were getting at earlier on in this conversation, which is that we're studying something cognitive here.
sentences.zh: 你在这次谈话早些时候提到的东西，那就是我们在这里研究的是认知方面的东西。

sentences.en: So we're interested in this cognitive skill and whether or not infants have it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对这种认知技能以及婴儿是否具备它很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And that is really their ability to detect incongruity, which means an unusual or unexpected event and to appraise it.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是他们检测不协调的能力，这意味着一种不寻常或意想不到的事件，并对其进行评估。

sentences.en: And what are they using in their environment to appraise it?
sentences.zh: 他们利用环境中的什么来评估它？

sentences.en: So that's, uh, the language that we use in funding.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们在申请资金时使用的语言。

sentences.en: So what are you studying now?
sentences.zh: 那你现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: What are the big questions that you're still trying to answer?
sentences.zh: 你还在试图回答哪些重大问题？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we just finished up a study.
sentences.zh: 我们刚完成了一项研究。

sentences.en: We have a manuscript in revision, fingers crossed that that's all done pretty soon.
sentences.zh: 我们有一份手稿正在修改中，祈祷很快就能全部完成。

sentences.en: One of the questions that I was really intrigued by was how infants differentiate different types of incongruities.
sentences.zh: 我非常感兴趣的问题之一是婴儿如何区分不同类型的不协调。

sentences.en: So there's a big body of literature that looks at magical incongruities.
sentences.zh: 有一个庞大的文献体系研究“神奇的不协调”。

sentences.en: These are impossible events, like a ball floating in the air, for example, um, or an object turning into another object.
sentences.zh: 这些是不可能的事件，比如一个球在空中漂浮，或者一个物体变成了另一个物体。

sentences.en: So we call them magical because these are kind of impossible events.
sentences.zh: 所以我们称它们为神奇的，因为这些是不可能的事件。

sentences.en: And there's a whole wonderful body of literature that shows that starting at about three and
sentences.zh: 有一个非常棒的文献体系表明，从大约3个半月大开始，

sentences.en: a half months of age, babies stare at those events when you compare those to control events.
sentences.zh: 当你将这些事件与对照事件进行比较时，婴儿会盯着这些事件看。

sentences.en: So they're really captivated by them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们真的被它们吸引住了。

sentences.en: Um, and then in my line of research, which is like four people doing this work, we show babies incongruities, but they're silly incongruities.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我的研究领域，就像有四个人在做这项工作，我们向婴儿展示不协调，但它们是“愚蠢的不协调”。

sentences.en: So the question that we've just gone after is how do babies distinguish these types of events?
sentences.zh: 所以我们刚刚追求的问题是婴儿如何区分这些类型的事件？

sentences.en: You know, can they?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们能吗？

sentences.en: And what we did in this last study was we presented babies with magical incongruities, but we put them in different contexts.
sentences.zh: 我们在最近这项研究中所做的是，向婴儿展示了神奇的不协调现象，但我们将它们置于不同的背景中。

sentences.en: Um, in the magic literature, babies just see the events there's, they don't see a person.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在魔术文献中，婴儿看到的只是事件本身，他们看不到人。

sentences.en: They just see hands or they see a theater screen where the events are unfolding in an asocial context.
sentences.zh: 他们看到的只是手，或者是一个正在上演这些事件的剧场屏幕，这是一种非社交背景。

sentences.en: So all we did was take two magic tricks and we put them in a social context.
sentences.zh: 所以我们所做的就是选取了两个魔术，并将它们置于社交背景中。

sentences.en: We had a magician perform the events.
sentences.zh: 我们让一位魔术师来表演这些事件。

sentences.en: They did not interact with the babies and babies were much more likely to smile at these events.
sentences.zh: 魔术师并没有与婴儿互动，但婴儿在面对这些事件时更有可能微笑。

sentences.en: They, they actually did not look longer at these events, uh, which contradicts this other body of literature, but it's one study.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上并没有在这些事件上停留更长时间，这与另一部分文献相矛盾，但这只是一项研究。

sentences.en: It's in a naturalistic context needs to be replicated, but it is interesting to think that, you know, infants are really, really picking up on the social environment and that
sentences.zh: 这需要在自然背景下进行重复验证，但想到婴儿确实在非常敏锐地感知社交环境，这一点很有趣，而且

sentences.en: they're deriving meaning about events just based on the presence of another person.
sentences.zh: 他们仅仅基于另一个人的存在，就能从事件中推导出意义。

sentences.en: And it could be, it could be that they're attributing intentionality, like, oh, that person meant to do that.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为他们赋予了事件意图性，比如，哦，那个人是故意那样做的。

sentences.en: And that lets them resolve the incongruity, which is like getting the punchline, like, oh, that's what you meant.
sentences.zh: 这让他们能够化解这种不协调感，就像听懂了笑话的梗一样，哦，原来你是这个意思。

sentences.en: That's funny.
sentences.zh: 真有趣。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: So I'm just working on our next study with a brilliant colleague, John Lane at Vanderbilt's.
sentences.zh: 所以我正在和范德堡大学一位出色的同事约翰·莱恩合作进行下一项研究。

sentences.en: He's been a consultant on this current study.
sentences.zh: 他一直是我们这项当前研究的顾问。

sentences.en: And, um, we're thinking about putting this question of intentionality really to the test and showing infants, uh, magic tricks where the magician will use a technique that again,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们正在考虑真正测试一下这个意图性问题，向婴儿展示魔术，魔术师会再次使用一种技巧，

sentences.en: Elena Hoica at the UK Bristol university has, uh, used where infants hear one of two verbal cues.
sentences.zh: 英国布里斯托大学的埃琳娜·霍伊卡曾使用过这种技巧，婴儿会听到两个口头提示中的一个。

sentences.en: They either hear the magician say, uh-oh, like this was a mistake or ha-ha, like I meant to do that.
sentences.zh: 他们要么听到魔术师说“哎呀”，表示这是一个失误，要么听到“哈哈”，表示我是故意那样做的。

sentences.en: And seeing if infants can use those cues to, uh, understand the intentionality of the magician
sentences.zh: 看看婴儿是否能利用这些提示来理解魔术师的意图，

sentences.en: in one condition and whether or not they'll be more likely to laugh in response or smile.
sentences.zh: 在一种情况下，看看他们是否更有可能做出大笑或微笑的反应。

sentences.en: So Elena's done something like that with older toddlers.
sentences.zh: 埃琳娜已经在年龄较大的幼儿身上做过类似的研究了。

sentences.en: Um, so we'd really be, uh, scaling it back for babies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们确实会将其规模缩小，针对婴儿进行研究。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Moreau, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，莫罗博士，感谢您今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: This was really a lot of fun and got me laughing too.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣，也让我笑个不停。

sentences.en: Oh, great.
sentences.zh: 哦，太好了。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, that's always a great success.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那总是一个巨大的成功。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your intereSt.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您的关注。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org，或者在 Apple、Spotify、YouTube 或任何您获取播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》往期节目。
